sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section connects the haftarah of Shabbos Chazon to the sin of the Golden Calf, explaining that the ox knew its Master through the holy name Yeli, but Israel did not know or contemplate this, leading them to err.

translations.translation: And this can be connected with what is said in the haftarah of Shabbos Chazon:
"An ox knows its owner... Israel does not know, My people does not contemplate."
And the Arizal explained
[today is the eve of his yahrtzeit],
that "ox" refers to the calf that the Erev Rav made in the desert,
by casting the tablet upon which Moshe had written "Ascend, ox," in order to raise Yosef's coffin.
And he explains,
that on this tablet was written the name Yeli
(the second name of the 72-letter name),
which is the appointee over the power of the supernal ox.
And this is "An ox knows its owner... Israel does not know...",
that the ox itself knew that it came from a holy name,
and Israel did not know, "My people did not contemplate,"
they did not know and did not contemplate this,
and they said that the calf ascended on its own, and therefore they erred after it.
And this is that the initials of "Israel does not know, My people does not contemplate" are Yeli Alah,
that they did not know and did not contemplate that this "ascended"
(the ox)
was through the name Yeli,
and therefore they said that it ascended on its own.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the interpretation of "Israel does not know" is a merit for Israel, as their sin stemmed from a lack of contemplation of matters beyond the world, leading to a limited revelation and ultimately the breaking of the tablets.

translations.translation: And it can be said,
that this explanation of "Israel does not know, My people does not contemplate" is a merit for Israel.
For the reason that they erred after the calf
was because they did not contemplate the matters
(the name Yeli)
that are above the world,
meaning that even then they served Havayah,
except that since it was before the commandment that "each day they should be as new in your eyes,"
therefore their service was with limitation,
and therefore,
the revelation that shone upon them then was only the light that is enclothed in the world.
And from this it devolved that they erred after the calf.
And this is also that the sin of the calf caused the breaking of the tablets, through which the possibility of forgetting the Torah came about,
meaning that even after the sin their connection with the Torah remained,
and only the study of Torah after the breaking of the tablets is with limitation, therefore interruption applies to it
(forgetting).
And through this the possibility was created that a nation and tongue would rule over them,
for when the revelation is only from the aspect of Malchus,
there is a place for exile,
as above.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the verse "Remember, Havayah, what has befallen us," that Havayah became like Elokim, and in man's service this means that even supernatural success is perceived as natural, which can lead to the error of attributing it to one's own power, as with the calf.

translations.translation: And this is what is said:
"Remember, Havayah, what has befallen us,"
and the Tzemach Tzedek explains
that "what" is the name Havayah
(in the spelling of Alpin, its gematria is 45),
and "us" has the gematria of Elokim,
and the explanation of "what has befallen us" is,
that Havayah became in the aspect of Elokim.
And it can be said,
that the matter of "what has befallen us" in man's service is,
that Havayah is above nature and Elokim has the gematria of nature,
that even when a person has success that is above nature, he thinks it is nature.
And moreover,
that sometimes,
the success that is above nature causes him to think that "his power and the might of his hand have made him this wealth,"
[similar to what happened with the calf,
that this that through the name Yeli the ascent of the ox was made
(a matter above nature)
brought them to think that it ascended on its own].
